# Strict Visual QA Verdict: FAIL

This capture does not show a procedural cloud sky at all. It fails on nearly every criterion.

## 1) Discrete clouds / gaps
**FAIL.** There are **zero** distinct clouds. The entire frame is a uniform pale lavender-gray haze with no visible sky, no cumulus shapes, and no blue-sky gaps. Instead we see editor gizmos: a white cube primitive with a label chip and shadow disc near center (~x 460–550, y 100–165), a teal wireframe camera frustum on the right (~x 650–860, y 95–280), a dark camera body at bottom right, and a viewport shading sphere top-right. The "cloud coverage 0.25" target is not even rendered — cloud count: **0**.

## 2) Lit vs. shadow shading
**FAIL.** No cloud tops or undersides exist to evaluate. The only lit/shaded read is on the cube, which is irrelevant.

## 3) Sky color
**FAIL.** Not blue in any region. The background is a washed-out, desaturated pale gray-lilac — the opposite of "rich blue with deeper zenith." No horizon gradient is discernible; if there is a gradient it is imperceptibly weak (slightly lighter at bottom-left, essentially flat).

## 4) Artifacts
- No streaks, speckle, or horizon blowout band — but only because no sky is rendered.
- What looks like faint soft blobs (e.g., left side ~x 20–120, y 20–80; bottom-left ~y 250–310) are either blur artifacts or stray geometry — indeterminate and unphotographic.

## 5) Photographic plausibility
**FAIL.** This is a raw editor viewport screenshot, not a sky render: UI label, wireframe frustum, gizmo sphere, and a shadow-catcher plane under the cube. Nothing here could pass as a photograph.

## Summary / action items
The cloud/sky pass appears not to be active in this view (wrong camera, sky layer disabled, or clouds below/beyond frame). Fix: re-render with the sky visible; then re-check discrete cloud separation at coverage 0.25, ambient/blue-sky color gradient, and top-light/underside-shade contrast before resubmitting.
